items.title: The fixed-endpoint second variation of a time-dependent action at a curve
items.reference: batch-12-local-construction; the fixed-endpoint family of D. Cline, Variational Principles, Sections 5.1-5.2, materialised as a definition and recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: The one-parameter fixed-endpoint family q+epsilon*eta of a C^2 curve and variation in a time-dependent Lagrangian chart, and the second variation delta^2 S(q)[eta,eta] as the second derivative at epsilon=0 of S(q+epsilon*eta); well-definedness (twice differentiability with the Hessian integral formula) delegated to lem-cm-second-variation-formula via justified_by. No minimisation or physical interpretation is asserted.
items.strategy: Define the family and the second derivative with the chart and extension conventions of def-cm-time-dependent-lagrangian-and-action; state the well-definedness and its exact source without proving it here.

items.title: The second variation of a time-dependent action: twice differentiability of the fixed-endpoint family and the Hessian integral formula
items.reference: expansion-proofs.md#e19 (the second-order step that the prose section differentiates silently)
items.statement: For a C^2 time-dependent Lagrangian chart, a C^2 curve q and a C^2 variation eta: the map epsilon -> S(q+epsilon*eta) is C^2 on a neighbourhood of 0 and its second derivative equals the integral of the Hessian form of L along the family, with the symmetric cross term 2 sum L_{q_j v_k} eta_j eta'_k by Clairaut; at epsilon=0 this is delta^2 S(q)[eta,eta]. Proved by two applications of differentiation under the integral sign on a compact rectangle.
items.strategy: Apply the compact-rectangle differentiation theorem twice: the first epsilon-derivative is the first-variation integrand, the second is the chain-rule derivative of that integrand along the affine family, computed with the C^1 gradients L_q and L_v; symmetrise the mixed sums by Clairaut.

items.title: Second variation of the oscillator action on a finite interval: both signs beyond the first conjugate time, and the degenerate value at $T=\\pi/\\omega$
items.statement: For L=(v^2-omega^2 q^2)/2 on [0,T], the zero curve is stationary and delta^2 S(q_0)[eta_n,eta_n]=(T/2)((n pi/T)^2-omega^2) for eta_n=sin(n pi t/T), with S(epsilon*eta_n)=(epsilon^2/2)delta^2 S exactly. If T>pi/omega the second variation is negative for n=1 and positive for every n>omega T/pi, so arbitrarily small variations both increase and decrease the action: the zero curve is neither a local minimiser nor a local maximiser. If T=pi/omega, the n=1 value is 0 while all n>=2 values are positive.
items.strategy: Compute the second variation with the Hessian formula, evaluate the elementary trigonometric integrals by the fundamental theorem of calculus, obtain the exact action along the family from the degree-two homogeneity of L, and read off the signs using the Archimedean property to select a large n.

items.title: The undamped oscillator on a conjugate-time interval: a one-dimensional Dirichlet solution space despite unique initial-value solutions
items.statement: For m,k>0 and omega=(k/m)^{1/2}: x_A=A sin(omega t) solves m x''+k x=0 with x_A(0)=0 and x_A(T)=A sin(omega T). If T=n pi/omega (n>=1) the set of C^2 solutions of the Dirichlet problem x(0)=x(T)=0 is exactly the one-dimensional space {A sin(omega t)}, so the boundary-value problem has infinitely many distinct solutions, while every initial-value problem has exactly one solution on R. For the chart L=(v^2-omega^2 q^2)/2 the same family is exactly the set of stationary curves with zero endpoints.
items.strategy: Verify the explicit family by differentiation, determine its endpoint values from the zero set of the sine, classify all Dirichlet solutions through the oscillator solution classification theorem, and identify stationarity with the Euler-Lagrange expression.

items.title: The inertia tensor of a mass distribution about an arbitrary point of $\\mathbb R^3$
items.reference: expansion-proofs.md#e19 (the shifted integrand of the parallel-axis computation, materialised as a definition and recorded in the batch notes)
items.statement: For a bounded finite Borel measure nu on R^3 and a point a, the shifted integrand G_a(rho)=||rho-a||_2^2 I_3-(rho-a)(rho-a)^T and the inertia tensor I_nu(a) with entries the Lebesgue integrals of the components of G_a; I_nu(0)=I(nu); entries are finite under AC_omega by lem-cm-inertia-tensor-about-a-point-is-finite (declared via justified_by). No physical body or unit system is asserted.
items.strategy: Define the shifted integrand and its componentwise integral against the measure with the conventions of def-cm-mass-distribution-and-inertia-matrix; declare the finiteness result that makes the entries well-defined.

items.title: Finiteness and a uniform bound for the entries of the inertia tensor about an arbitrary point
items.reference: batch-12-local-construction; the finiteness/boundedness step added to make the shifted inertia tensor well-defined, recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: Assume AC_omega. For a finite bounded Borel measure nu with nu(R^3 minus closed ball of radius R)=0, every component of the shifted integrand is Borel measurable and nu-integrable, and |I_nu(a)_{jk}| <= 2(R+||a||_2)^2 nu(R^3). The axiom is used once, through the published measurability criterion for continuous maps.
items.strategy: Prove measurability of the continuous polynomial integrands, bound the integrand on the support ball by the constant 2(R+||a||)^2 using the triangle inequality and the elementary inequality 2uv<=u^2+v^2, and integrate the constant against the finite measure.

items.title: Parallel-axis theorem: the inertia tensor about a displaced point of a centred mass distribution
items.statement: Assume AC_omega. For a centred mass distribution nu on R^3 of total mass m, the inertia tensor about any point a satisfies I_nu(a)=I(nu)+m(||a||_2^2 I_3-a a^T), entrywise I_nu(a)_{jk}=I(nu)_{jk}+m(||a||_2^2 delta_{jk}-a_j a_k). Proved by expanding the shifted integrand into the parent integrand, constants and first-moment terms, integrating termwise and using centredness.
items.strategy: Expand ||rho-a||^2 and (rho-a)(rho-a)^T, integrate the finite real combination termwise by L^1 linearity, and cancel the first-moment terms by the centredness hypothesis.

items.title: Two equal masses with two outer springs and a coupling spring: eigenmodes, decoupling and the explicit normal frequencies
items.statement: For m>0, k>=0, c>=0 and K=[[k+c,-c],[-c,k+c]]: K u_+ = k u_+ and K u_- = (k+2c) u_- for u_+-(1,1)/sqrt2, u_-=(1,-1)/sqrt2, which are orthonormal; the system m x''=-Kx is equivalent through x=y_+ u_+ + y_- u_- to the two scalar oscillator equations m y_+''+k y_+=0 and m y_-''+(k+2c)y_-=0, with unique pair y_pm=<u_pm,x>; for k>0 the solutions are superpositions of an in-phase mode with squared frequency k/m and an anti-phase mode with squared frequency (k+2c)/m. If k=0 the u_+ mode is affine and unbounded for nonzero slope.
items.strategy: Verify the eigenrelations and orthonormality by matrix multiplication, prove the decoupling bijection by pulling the system back along the eigenbasis and conversely reassembling two scalar solutions, and read the scalar solution families off the oscillator classification theorem.

items.title: The pendulum field near the downward equilibrium: bounded force derivative, cubic remainder and the finite-time small-angle error bound
items.reference: expansion-proofs.md#e19 (the E8 instantiation θ''=-(g/l) sin θ with cubic remainder)
items.statement: For g,l>0, omega=(g/l)^{1/2} and F(theta,v)=(v,-omega^2 sin theta): F is C^infinity with A=DF(0)=[[0,1],[-omega^2,0]], ||F(z)-Az||_2=omega^2|sin theta - theta| <= (omega^2/6)|theta|^3 <= (omega^2 r/6)||z||_2^2 and ||F(z)||_2<=L||z||_2 with L=max{1,omega^2}=||A|| on ||z||<=r; F is globally Lipschitz with constant L. For delta e^{LT}<r the maximal solution exists on [0,T] and ||z(t)-y(t)||_2 <= (omega^2 r/6) delta^2 int_0^t e^{||A||(t-s)} e^{2Ls} ds <= (omega^2 r/6) delta^2 t e^{(||A||+2L)t}, where y solves the linearised (exactly harmonic) pendulum. The estimate is finite-time and of order delta^2.
items.strategy: Compute the total derivative of F, bound the quadratic remainder by the cubic Taylor estimate for the sine, identify the Lipschitz and operator norms, and instantiate thm-cm-finite-time-linearization-error-bound.

items.title: Scope and limits of the verification items on this page
items.reference: batch-12-local-construction; scope record for the verification items, recorded in the batch notes

items.statement: Scope of the verification items: all are mathematics with no physical or empirical content; the second-variation sign results are finite-time statements about the action functional; the degeneracy at T=pi/omega concerns an underdetermined boundary-value problem; the parallel-axis theorem is the centred case; the coupled-oscillator statement is exact for the linear system; the pendulum bound is finite-time, conditional and of order delta^2, and asserts no exact harmonicity of the nonlinear model.
items.strategy: Record the limits that are part of the claims and their provenance, so consumers carry them; no proof obligation.

items.title: An explicit saddle of the oscillator action at $T=2\\pi$: the two variations $\\sin(t/2)$ and $\\sin(3t/2)$
items.reference: batch-12-constructed-B-example; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: At omega=1, T=2pi: delta^2 S(q_0)[sin(t/2),sin(t/2)]=-3pi/4 and delta^2 S(q_0)[sin(3t/2),sin(3t/2)]=5pi/4, with exact action values S(epsilon eta_1)=-3pi epsilon^2/8<0<5pi epsilon^2/8=S(epsilon eta_3); the defining integrals are also evaluated directly. The stationary zero curve is a saddle at this duration.
items.strategy: Substitute T=2pi and omega=1 in the second-variation formula, evaluate the two trigonometric integrals independently as a check, and read the saddle behaviour off the exact action identity.

items.strategy: Verify the two solutions and their boundary data, note distinctness and the differing initial velocities, and evaluate the action along the family with the double-angle formula and the fundamental theorem of calculus.

items.title: Two-mass spring eigenmodes at explicit parameters: eigenrelations, a mode solution, and the zero-frequency case
items.reference: batch-12-constructed-B-example; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: At m=1, k=1, c=3: K=[[4,-3],[-3,4]] satisfies K u_+ = u_+ and K u_- = 7 u_-, so the squared frequencies are 1 and 7; the curve cos(t)u_+ + cos(sqrt7 t)u_- solves x''=-Kx with x(0)=(sqrt2,0), x'(0)=0. At k=0, c=1 the curve (1+t)u_+ solves x''=-Kx and is unbounded.

items.title: The pendulum linearisation bound at $g=l=1$: exact error expression for the data $\\delta=1/100$, $T=1$
items.reference: batch-12-constructed-B-example; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: At g=l=1, r=1/2, delta=1/100, T=1 the condition delta e^{LT}<r follows from 2<e<3; the linearisation bound gives ||z(t)-y(t)||_2 <= (e^{2t}-e^t)/(12*10^4) on [0,1] with y(t)=delta(cos t,-sin t), at most e^3/(12*10^4) at t=1, and the pointwise remainder bounds |sin theta - theta|<=1/48, |sin theta|<=1/2 hold on the ball.
items.strategy: Instantiate the proposition at the stated constants, verify the smallness condition with the published bound on e, evaluate the integral by the fundamental theorem, and check the pointwise remainder bounds.
